canonical_title: US AI infrastructure debt issuance begins testing investor limits
treatment: Do not repeat general AI capex/debt commentary. Reinclude only for a material new issuance, failed/downsized deal, sharp pricing change, rating action, or quantified investor-capacity shift.
known_facts: Reuters reported on August 21 that investors are demanding larger yield concessions as AI-related corporate bond supply surges.
BNP Paribas data cited by Reuters put 2026 AI hyperscaler debt issuance at $220 billion as of August 10, versus $12.5 billion in the comparable 2025 period.
Amazon's recent $25 billion long-dated bond sale priced around 120 basis points over Treasuries, roughly twice the comparable spread a year earlier according to analysts cited by Reuters.
Tech corporate bond spreads were reported at 89 basis points, 9 basis points wider than the overall investment-grade market.
Institutional portfolio concentration limits of roughly 2% to 3% per issuer were identified as a practical constraint if repeated hyperscaler issuance continues.

Wall Street Journal's October 31 reporting says CoreWeave, Nebius and Nscale have faced severely restricted bond-market access as lenders tighten terms; it also reports Lambda lowered its target valuation. This is a reported financing-access signal, not proof that any firm is insolvent or that every deal is cancelled.
reinclude_only_if: A major AI-related bond issue fails, is downsized, or requires materially larger concessions.
A hyperscaler or major AI infrastructure borrower receives a material rating/outlook change tied to AI capex.
New market data shows a material change in AI debt issuance volume, spreads, or institutional capacity.
A named neocloud secures or loses a material debt facility, changes valuation materially, or announces a confirmed new credit guarantee.
notes: Selected because the quantified market-capacity signal became visible after the midday cutoff; this is not a model release but materially changes interpretation of AI infrastructure financing conditions. 2026-10-31 night: FOLLOW_UP based on WSJ's named, cross-company lending-access details surfaced after midday JST; Nscale IPO postponement was already reported on Oct 22, so it is not counted as a new event. No formal default/rating action established.
